So, the part about this article that fascinated me is that a weird mix of different ingredients go into this massive pot with a child, and out comes the Elixer of Life, as it was. There is another anomaly with similar properties in SCP-2077 in which odd ingredients are used to make pills with regenerative properties. Seems resonable to make a connection that some of the ingreditents of those pills might be ingredients used to form Liquid Life. As such, I am proposing the following edit:

Changing this:

Ingredients list, including such materials as live leeches, skullcap seeds, chicken fetuses, snake skin, ginger root, mandrake root, lily-of-the-valley-water, spider eggs, and nearly two dozen more items, in varying amounts. The most prominent ingredient appears to be a living human being, preferably a child.

To this:

Ingredients list, including such materials as live leeches, skullcap seeds, chicken fetuses, snake skin, ginger root, mandrake root, lily-of-the-valley-water, spider eggs, and nearly two dozen more items, in varying amounts. The most prominent ingredient appears to be a living human being, preferably a child. Multiple ingredients on this list have been noted to match the ingredients used in instances of SCP-2077

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: Re: Is op still around? I have a grammatical revision.
item.content:encoded:
In my opinion this is just a punctuation error, taking the following sentence into account too.

As it stands now it's:
"Despite appearing to be 80+ years old, 545-A is in exceptional health, with no weakening of the heart, bones, or respiratory system, and although of average human strength. Her senses are noted to be above-average, and she scores a general 115 on a standard IQ test."

Although I think it was intended to be this:
"Despite appearing to be 80+ years old, 545-A is in exceptional health, with no weakening of the heart, bones, or respiratory system. And although of average human strength, her senses are noted to be above-average and she scores a general 115 on a standard IQ test."

There are a couple of more ", and" problems and such. Is the creator going to fix these any time soon? And if not, can any of us get permission to fix the grammar?

Either way. Downvoted until this gets a tone change.

item.title: Is op still around? I have a grammatical revision.

I take issue with the grammar in the following passage.

[ Despite appearing to be 80+ years old, 545-A is in exceptional health, with no weakening of the heart, bones, or respiratory system, and although of average human strength.]

"…and although…"

Suggested revision would have the passage instead reading; " Despite appearing to be 80+ years old, 545-A is in exceptional health, with no weakening of the heart, bones, or respiratory system, and seems to be of average human strength despite her advanced age."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
What do you think "magic" means?

"Magic" is a state of mind. "Magic" is a word that means "we accept that we do not understand this, we accept that we will never be able to understand it, we accept that it is intrinsically not something that can be understood, ever, by anyone."

There is no magic in the real world because the scientific mindset tells us that everything can eventually be understood and explained — even if not by us, then eventually by our descendants. There is no magic in the real world because we do not accept that anything can be magic. We understand that "magic" is just a weakness in definition. If something exists, it can, ultimately, be understood. If something exists, it is not magic.

If you want magic in your world, just accept that things are magic. Accept that your microwave and smartphone and chemotherapy are magic; accept that caterpillars turn into butterflies because of incantations, and that eclipses are caused by demons trying to eat the sun.

The Foundation rejects this mindset utterly. "It's magic" is not an explanation with any predictive power. "Anomalous" is not just a more scientific-sounding way of saying the same thing, it's a way of saying "we don't understand how this works, it doesn't make any sense according to all our knowledge of how everything else in the universe works, nothing we've tried has made any sense so far… but we're sure that someday, somehow, we will figure it out."

"Magic" is "don't know, don't care". "Anomalous" is "don't know, care very very much."
